   We will also say that f is strongly convex in V , if there exists λ > 0 and a norm such

  From the definition, it is clear that if a function is λ-strongly convex, it is also λ′ -strongly
convex for any 0 ≤ λ′ < λ. Moreover, convex functions are 0-strongly convex.

   In Follow-the-Regularized-Leader (FTRL), in each round we output the minimizer of
the regularized cumulative past losses, see Algorithm 7.1. It should be clear that FTRL is not
an algorithm, but a family of algorithms, in the same way that Online Mirror Descent (OMD)
is a family of algorithms.
   Before analyzing FTRL, let’s get some intuition on it. In OMD, we saw that the “state”
of the algorithm is stored in the current iterate xt , in the sense that the next iterate xt+1
depends on xt and the loss received at time t, plus obviously the choice of the learning rate.
Instead, in FTRL, the next iterate xt+1 depends on the entire history of losses received up to
time t and on the regularizer used at time t. This has an immediate consequence: in the case
that V is bounded, OMD will only “remember” the last xt and nothing else. On the other
hand, FTRL keeps in memory the entire history of the past, which in principle allows us to
recover the iterates before the projection in V .
   This difference in behavior might make the reader think that FTRL is more computation-
